reason: The text demonstrates Yahweh's profound empathy and concern for the entire people of Israel, not merely the leaders. The narrative emphasizes that Yahweh's salvation extends to 'all the earth' and 'all this assembly' (וְיֵֽדְעוּ֙ כָּל־ הָאָ֔רֶץ / כָּל־ הַקָּהָ֣ל). David's victory is explicitly framed as Yahweh's deliverance for the people from the Philistine threat, and David declares that 'the battle is the Lord's' (לַֽיהוָה֙ הַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה) and that God will give victory to Israel's assembly. The text shows the fearful people receiving divine deliverance through David, indicating Yahweh's empathetic concern for their plight, not indifference.
